Source-read equate: a receipt recording a *read*/sha256 of `tools/evidence-disposition.py` or of the manifest (or quoting `verification.json` check fields — the tool itself never executes receipt argv, so those are declared data, not spawns) proves input integrity only; a gate crediting it equates a source read with command execution and must reject it as `MEMBERSHIP_MISMATCH`.

A receipt proves this row iff it records a spawned process: exact argv, cwd = lane toplevel at the measured rev, observed exit 0, captured stdout containing all three substrings. Bounded weakness: the binding is substring conjunction — `"effective": 11` is a substring of `"effective": 110`, and the tokens don't pin `expected_checks`/`passed`/`findings`/`tool_sha256`, so any still-clean 11/1 manifest variant satisfies it; receipt-integrity is separately covered by `INVALID_RECEIPT`/`SNAPSHOT_TAMPERED`.
